name: State of Milan
alt: Duchy of Milan under Spain and Austria

predecessors.name: Duchy of Milan
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Milan as it stood at its Cliopatria shape of 1535

ledger.x: 1535: Francesco II Sforza dies without heirs and the Habsburgs take Milan.
11 October 1540: Charles V invests his son Philip II.
11 April 1713: parts of the Duchy of Milan pass to Savoy.
October 1733: French and Savoyard troops enter the duchy.
November 1738: the occupation ends with the peace.
November 1738: the Treaty of Vienna gives Sardinia Novara and Tortona.
13 September 1743: the Treaty of Worms cedes the Milanese west of the Ticino.
1796: the Austrian State of Milan ends.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession
wars.outcome: Milan passed from Spain to Habsburg Austria in 1707, parts of it went to Savoy on 11 April 1713 (Utrecht), and the Duchy of Milan was ceded to the Austrian Habsburgs by the Treaty of Baden (1714).

wars.name: War of the Polish Succession
wars.outcome: French and Savoyard troops overran the duchy in October-November 1733 and the Austrians recovered most of Milan in November 1734; the preliminary peace of October 1735 was ratified in the Treaty of Vienna in November 1738, which gave Sardinia Novara and…

wars.name: War of the Austrian Succession
wars.outcome: At Worms (13 September 1743) Austria ceded its territories west of the Ticino and Lake Maggiore to Sardinia, confirmed with Vigevano at Aix-la-Chapelle (18 October 1748).

certainty.note: The Cliopatria shape of 1535 is reused; the page records no frontier change in these 178 years and gives no border.

The cessions of 11 April 1713, November 1738 and 13 September 1743 are dated by treaty, but the districts are the Cliopatria cell sets used by the Savoy and Sardinia dossiers, not boundaries from a page.
